# Double descent: final test loss versus model width

This graph sweeps a one-hidden-layer ReLU MLP over width on one **fixed** noisy regression dataset. Each width is trained independently. The analysis chain selects the test-loss history, slices its last logged value, and appends that scalar with the matching `model.width` metadata to the sweep table.

**Run:** click the Trainer once. Its comma-separated `width` field launches every width sequentially. When it finishes, the only deliverable is the plot at right: **final test MSE vs model.width**.

**Expected signature:** test loss decreases at small width, rises near the first widths that interpolate the noisy training set, then decreases again in the overparameterized regime. Keep the dataset seed, model seed, noise, training budget, optimizer, and all non-width fields fixed.

**If no peak appears:** confirm every width has converged, then increase `noiseLevel` to 0.75 or 1.0 or reduce `trainSize` to 64. A single seed is an exploratory reproduction, not a robust statistical claim.

## Result pipeline

`training_visualization` exposes the rank-1 `test_loss` history. `tensor_selector` chooses it; `tensor_slicing` uses index `-1` to reduce it to final test MSE; `tensor_viz_0d` supplies the scalar; and `sweep_data_table` records it with the current `model.width`.

After the trainer completes every width, inspect only **Final test MSE vs model width**. The table keeps the width/scalar rows even though the trainer overwrites ordinary visualization histories when it moves to the next width. Clear the sweep table before starting a changed experiment so stale rows are not mixed into the new curve.
